newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline firms, helped by Texaco run cuts.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline firms, helped by Texaco run cuts.

text.p: NWE gasoline barges were firmer on Thursday, supported by news of refinery run cuts in Rotterdam, traders said.

Eurograde barges traded at $203.50 in the morning and a bid was heard shortly before lunchtime, for Rotterdam refinery material, at $203. "There is very little gasoline available in Europe at the moment," one refiner said.
Traders said Texaco Rotterdam had cut crude throughput by 20 percent at its 400,000 barrels per day (bpd) Nerefco refinery and this had reduced their spot availabilities of gasoline.

The company was heard to have withdrawn from selling gasoline on the spot market but a trader at the refinery declined to say by how much throughput had been cut. "We will have to wait and see how far the reduction goes," he said.

Complex refinery margins in Rotterdam fell to around $1.30 a barrel on Thursday from last week's average of $2, and while no other refiners were known to have cut back yet, Total's 148,000 bpd Flushing refinery was under pressure to do so, trade sources said.
